selection_policy: Curated operators with public primary financial disclosures. Sixteen historical comparison records include listed companies and one private IPO applicant; three additional private operators are an unranked coverage watchlist. Not an exhaustive market census.
coupon_selection_policy: Multiple reviewed USD fixed-note examples per company where reliable primary terms exist. Instruments are sortable, never company health/cost ranks. Some notes are confirmed at the company snapshot, others only at earlier dates; status and principal dates are explicit. This is not a complete security inventory.
method_notes: Borrowings are consolidated carrying values net of disclosed discounts/costs, excluding both operating and finance lease liabilities. They are not total liabilities or face principal.
Borrowings/assets uses the same reporting date for numerator and denominator. Every row retains its own date; no pro forma post-quarter updates are mixed in.
Cash is balance-sheet cash and cash equivalents, not total liquidity; restricted balances, investments and crypto assets are excluded where separately disclosed.
Compare business models carefully. A default AI-infrastructure group includes both GPU clouds and mixed transition businesses. Landlords and bitcoin miners are separate filters.
No health score, buy/sell recommendation, bond market yield or real-time quote feed is supplied.

debt.title: Recorded borrowings
debt.description: How big is the borrowing balance? This is the amount recorded for loans and notes, with leases left out.
debt.formula: Short-term + long-term recorded borrowings, excluding leases
debt.caveat: The recorded balance can differ from the principal required by the debt contract because of discounts, fees and other accounting adjustments. Operating and finance leases are excluded but remain real obligations. A larger balance does not establish repayment ability; some project debt has limited claims on the parent company.

debt_assets.title: Borrowings / assets
debt_assets.description: How large are borrowings relative to the company’s recorded assets? Read the percentage as dollars of borrowing for every $100 of assets.
debt_assets.formula: Reported borrowings ÷ total assets × 100, from the same reporting date
debt_assets.caveat: Assets are not the same as cash available to repay debt. This ratio does not show which assets were financed with borrowing or predict default. Leased infrastructure, crypto holdings and construction assets make company comparisons imperfect. Assets can include the recorded right to use leased property, while the borrowing measure excludes lease obligations.

coupon.title: Bond coupon examples
coupon.description: What fixed interest rate is written into this specific note? Each row is one debt contract, not the company’s overall borrowing rate.
coupon.formula: Contractual fixed coupon for the named instrument; no blended borrowing-rate estimate
coupon.caveat: Coupon is not current market yield or total funding cost. Convertible, secured project and unsecured notes differ. One note does not represent all company debt. These are terms from dated disclosures; continued outstanding status has not been reverified for every example.

disclosure: Actual, dated source records. No synthetic financial inputs enter these rankings. This is a curated research snapshot, not a live market feed or credit rating.
